competences: The learner identifies and describes the main features of the national anthem from the source material.
The learner explains how the national anthem relates to Uganda's national identity.
languageCompetence: Learners pronounce, spell, read and write: Anthem, composer, stanza, patriotism, friendship, liberty, national unity.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify the main facts about the national anthem.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer at least four sourced questions correctly about the national anthem.
priorKnowledge: Learners know about the flag as a national symbol and have encountered the national anthem at school assemblies.
materials: Printed chart with Uganda's national anthem
Textbook reference on the anthem's three stanzas
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous work and asks: "Who composed the Uganda National Anthem?" Learners' first responses introduce the national anthem in the topic Uganda as an independent nation. The teacher establishes what learners already understand.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall earlier work about Uganda, answer the opening question and connect their responses with today's new sub-topic.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and history of the national anthem
steps.content: The national anthem is Uganda's official national song. It was composed by George Wilberforce Kakoma. The anthem was first officially performed on Independence Day. Uganda's anthem has three stanzas. It expresses the country's principles, hopes and goals. The national anthem promotes unity and patriotism.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher uses the printed chart with uganda's national anthem to teach meaning and history of the national anthem. They put the exact sourced points on the board: "The national anthem is Uganda's official national song. It was composed by George Wilberforce Kakoma." They check understanding with the question: "Why is Late. George William Kakoma remembered in the history of Uganda." and explain the relevant terms.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners observe the material, identify the listed facts, respond to the teacher's question and copy the organised notes into their exercise books.

source.quote: It was composed by George Wilberforce Kakoma.

steps.stage: Development: Messages in Uganda's national anthem
steps.content: The first stanza expresses belief in God. It calls on Ugandans to remain united and free. The second stanza speaks about peace and friendship. It expresses love and labour for the country. The third stanza describes fertile soil and sunshine. It reminds people of Uganda's rich natural environment.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher uses the printed chart with uganda's national anthem to teach messages in uganda's national anthem. They put the exact sourced points on the board: "The first stanza expresses belief in God. It calls on Ugandans to remain united and free." They check understanding with the question: "Give two reasons why Ugandans sing the national anthem" and explain the relevant terms.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners observe the material, identify the listed facts, respond to the teacher's question and copy the organised notes into their exercise books.

steps.stage: Development: Occasions when the national anthem is performed
steps.content: It is performed on school assemblies. It is performed during parliamentary sessions. It is performed at official ceremonies. It is performed at the opening of sports activities. It is performed during important public functions.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher uses the printed chart with uganda's national anthem to teach occasions when the national anthem is performed. They put the exact sourced points on the board: "It is performed on school assemblies. It is performed during parliamentary sessions." They check understanding with the question: "When was the national anthem played for the first time in Uganda?" and explain the relevant terms.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners observe the material, identify the listed facts, respond to the teacher's question and copy the organised notes into their exercise books.

steps.stage: Development: Respect and importance of the anthem
steps.content: People stand at attention during the national anthem. They remain still until its performance ends. The anthem promotes respect for Uganda. It encourages national identity and unity. It reminds citizens of their national duties. It also serves as a national prayer.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher uses the printed chart with uganda's national anthem to teach respect and importance of the anthem. They put the exact sourced points on the board: "People stand at attention during the national anthem. They remain still until its performance ends." They check understanding with the question: "How is the National Anthem respected when its being sung?" and explain the relevant terms.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners observe the material, identify the listed facts, respond to the teacher's question and copy the organised notes into their exercise books.
